ordered_diagnoses: Soft tissue metastasis from other primary sites

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging subcutaneous nodule with possible metastasis or primary soft tissue tumor
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging right-flank subcutaneous nodule over two years
Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules on chest CT
Multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 on abdominal CT
key_facts: 52-year-old man
HBV-positive hepatocellular carcinoma treated with partial hepatectomy, entecavir, transarterial chemoembolization, sorafenib, regorafenib, and pembrolizumab
Subcutaneous nodule over right hypochondriac and flank regions, approximately 8×4 cm
Vital signs: temperature 37.2°C, pulse 112/min, respiratory rate 19/min, blood pressure 114/78 mmHg
Denies alcohol or tobacco use
Laboratory studies: white blood cell count 8.93×10^3/µl, hemoglobin 13.8 g/dl, AST 55.7 U/l, ALT 55.7 U/l, lactate dehydrogenase 201 U/l, alpha-fetoprotein 157 ng/ml
CEA 7.99 ng/ml, CA19-9 21.6 U/ml, HBsAg reactive, HCV-PCR negative
Contrast-enhanced CT of chest revealed multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules
Abdominal CT showed multiple nodules in liver segments 5 and 7 and a right-flank soft tissue mass invading the 12th rib
